entries.source_title: Conjugate regular verbs in the subjunctive present in French (Le Subjonctif Présent)
entries.note: Regular endings and spelling were already substantial. Added stem transfer for indicative-irregular partir, écrire and lire, with full paradigms and independent singular/plural retrieval rather than treating irregularity as universal.

entries.source_title: Special cases when the past participle agrees (in number & gender) when used with 'avoir' in the compound past in French (Le Passé Composé)
entries.note: Preceding direct objects, relative que and indirect-object non-agreement already have contrasting examples and constructed practice. The existing infinitive, en and measurement boundaries add useful depth; no cosmetic expansion was needed.

entries.source_title: Conjugate être in the subjunctive present in French (Le Subjonctif Présent)
entries.note: The full être subjunctive series is already connected to ordinary requirements, with nous/vous spelling and several-person retrieval. A second standalone conjugation section would duplicate the consolidated lesson.

entries.source_title: Entrer can be used with avoir or être in compound tenses depending on its meaning in French (Le Passé Composé)
entries.note: Entering versus entering data was already clear. Added a more reliable object-finding procedure and a locative-y case so auxiliary choice no longer depends on spotting a noun immediately after the verb.

entries.source_title: Sortir can be used with avoir or être in Le Passé Composé depending on its meaning in French
entries.note: The baseline contrasted leaving and taking out, but not publication. Added publication as an intransitive or transitive event, with distinct publisher/publication subjects and independent auxiliary checks.

entries.source_title: Conjugate aller in the subjunctive present in French (Le Subjonctif Présent)
entries.note: Both aill- and all- stems, every person and natural contextual uses already appear together. Practice retrieves both stems rather than relying on recognition of a familiar singular.

entries.source_title: Conjugate faire in the subjunctive present in French (Le Subjonctif Présent)
entries.note: The fass- paradigm already includes independent nous, vous and on production and separates it from indicative fais- and future fer-. The comparison found no meaningful formation gap.

entries.source_title: Descendre can be used with avoir or être in compound tenses depending on its meaning in French (Le Passé Composé)
entries.note: Downward movement, cargo and a directly named route were already distinguished. Added a preceding object-pronoun case to connect auxiliary choice with participle agreement rather than the visible destination phrase.

entries.source_title: Conjugate avoir in the subjunctive present in French (Le Subjonctif Présent)
entries.note: Aie/aies/ait/ayons/ayez/aient are fully taught with spelling contrasts and several constructed persons. Existing explanation makes the auxiliary usable beyond isolated table recall.

entries.source_title: Monter can be used with avoir or être in Le Passé Composé depending on its meaning in French
entries.note: The assembly meaning was missing from an otherwise strong movement/route contrast. Added assembly examples and new tasks with both following objects and preceding feminine-plural objects.

entries.source_title: Conjugate prendre and derivatives in the subjunctive present in French (Le Subjonctif Présent)
entries.note: The prenn-/pren- decision already transfers across independently exercised derivatives. Full prendre/comprendre/apprendre series and meaningful contexts provide depth without enumerating every possible prefix.

entries.source_title: Conjugate cueillir and derivatives in the future tense in French (Le Futur Simple)
entries.note: The cueiller- future pattern, all six persons and meanings of cueillir/accueillir/recueillir are already explicit. Exercises apply the stem to all three verbs rather than only one memorized form.

entries.source_title: Il faut que + the subjunctive mood (Le Subjonctif) in French
entries.note: Impersonal necessity and the infinitive alternative were adequate. Added the practical distinction between prohibition and absence of necessity, so learners can make attendance optional without accidentally banning it.

entries.source_title: Retourner can be used with avoir or être in compound tenses depending on its meaning in French (Le Passé Composé)
entries.note: Retained the legitimate merchandise-return meaning excluded by the public source. Added an explicit supplier-return example and fresh task; the Académie transitive entry supports this use alongside turning over and going back.

references.purpose: Read transitive sense I.2, including returned unsold goods; checked the source's merchandise-return exclusion.

entries.source_title: Vouloir que + the subjunctive mood (Le Subjonctif) = To want someone to do something in French
entries.note: Same-subject infinitives, different-subject wishes and courteous voudrais que already have meaningful contrasts and production. The ordinary desire construction needs no extra table or duplicate drill.

entries.source_title: Conjugate pouvoir in the subjunctive present in French (Le Subjonctif Présent)
entries.note: All puiss- forms are available with ability/permission meanings and independent plural retrieval. The existing lesson avoids confusing the mood of pouvoir with whether a future action is possible.

entries.source_title: Rentrer can be used with avoir or être in compound tenses depending on its meaning in French (Le Passé Composé)
entries.note: Returning home and bringing objects indoors were adequate. Added a preceding direct-object task and locative-y contrast to expose the construction when its complement is not a following noun.

entries.source_title: Conjugate venir/tenir and derivatives in the subjunctive present in French (Le Subjonctif Présent)
entries.note: Complete venir/tenir patterns explain the two stem families and extend them to several derivatives in new contexts. Existing production checks both stem choices; further prefix lists would not add a new learner decision.

entries.source_title: Conjugate savoir in the subjunctive present in French (Le Subjonctif Présent)
entries.note: Savoir's full sach- series and its learned-ability meaning already have contextual examples and singular/plural construction tasks. Formation is distinct from the separate lesson on mood after savoir que.

entries.source_title: Aimer que/détester que + the subjunctive mood (Le Subjonctif) = to like/hate that in French
entries.note: Real emotional facts were already distinguished from uncertainty. Added negative aimer and negative-clause scope. The source also generalizes about negative opinions, explicitly including savoir; that side claim is not adopted, and explains the separate stance evidence and savoir reference here.

references.purpose: Checked the distinction between literary je ne sache pas que and ordinary savoir usage. This entry does not directly explain the full negative-savoir indicative contrast.

entries.source_title: Conjugate irregular être/avoir/savoir in the imperative mood in French (L'Impératif)
entries.note: The three imperative persons of être/avoir/savoir, missing subject pronouns and realistic awareness/register limits are already illustrated and exercised. The content does not imply that an imperative can instantly create learned ability.

entries.source_title: Repasser can be used with avoir or être in compound tenses depending on its meaning in French (Le Passé Composé)
entries.note: Kept the established intransitive avoir alternative instead of importing an absolute être rule. Added objectless ironing as a lexical counterexample to the 'no following noun' shortcut; the dictionary explicitly supports both boundaries.

references.purpose: Read the intransitive auxiliary-variation note and the absolute ironing use; checked an overbroad auxiliary split.

entries.source_title: J'allais + [infinitive] to express the near future in the past in French
entries.note: Past projection and uncertain fulfilment were strong, but literal travel was not contrasted. Added intention, movement in progress and completed trips for a purpose, without inferring that a trip guarantees its goal.

entries.source_title: Conjugate regular -er, -ir, -dre verbs (+ avoir) in the pluperfect tense in French (Le Plus-que-Parfait)
entries.note: The complete imperfect avoir series already combines with regular participle families in an earlier-past timeline. Negation and preceding-object agreement make the formation usable rather than merely listed.

entries.source_title: Conjugate être/avoir/faire/prendre/vouloir (+ avoir) in the pluperfect tense in French (Le Plus-que-Parfait)
entries.note: Each named irregular verb has its participle, auxiliary pattern and an independent constructed item. The lesson also explains why être itself uses avoir; a separate miniature lesson per verb would duplicate existing teaching.

entries.source_title: Conjugate verbs (+ être) in the pluperfect tense in French (Le Plus-que-Parfait)
entries.note: Earlier movement with être, subject agreement and the transitive movement exception are already connected. Examples and retrieval distinguish returning oneself from taking an object out, not just auxiliary memorization.

entries.source_title: Conjugate reflexive verbs in the pluperfect tense in French (Le Plus-que-Parfait)
entries.note: The full reflexive pluperfect series and negative order are adequate. Preserved the direct/indirect-object agreement distinction rather than the source's automatic subject-agreement generalization; s'étaient parlé remains valid.

references.purpose: Checked direct versus indirect reflexive objects and the absence of automatic subject agreement.

entries.source_title: Conjugate vouloir in the subjunctive present in French (Le Subjonctif Présent)
entries.note: The useful veuill-/voul- paradigm is complete and practised with natural concessive contexts. It is clearly separated from using a main-clause vouloir to select another verb's subjunctive; rare variants need not be routine production targets.

entries.source_title: Conjugate devoir in the pluperfect tense in French (Le Plus-que-Parfait)
entries.note: All persons of the pluperfect modal and dû spelling already support earlier necessity. The explicit contrast with retrospective conditional advice prevents a more consequential error than missing another conjugation example.

entries.source_title: Conjugate pouvoir in the pluperfect tense in French (Le Plus-que-Parfait)
entries.note: Earlier ability and realized opportunity are already distinguished from unrealized could-have meanings. The full auxiliary series and contextual pu tasks provide adequate formation and interpretation.

entries.source_title: Conjugate regular -er, -ir, -dre verbs (+ avoir) in the conditional past in French (Le Conditionnel Passé)
entries.note: Regular conditional formation and counterfactuals were deep, but unconfirmed reporting was only mentioned. Added attributed reports versus alternative pasts, with a new conditional construction task and a confirmation contrast.

entries.source_title: Conjugate verbs with irregular past participles in the conditional past in French (Le Conditionnel Passé)
entries.note: Irregular participles already appear with the full conditional auxiliary series and several independently constructed verbs. Counterfactual context and ordinary agreement are available in the same lesson; no formation gap remained.

entries.source_title: Conjugate verbs (+ être) in the conditional past in French (Le Conditionnel Passé)
entries.note: Être forms and reflexive agreement were adequate. Added the reported-information use with agreeing feminine-plural subjects and an independent arrival interpretation/confirmation sequence, not just another hypothetical journey.

entries.source_title: Conjugate devoir in the conditional past in French = should have (Le Conditionnel Passé)
entries.note: Retrospective advice, negative should-not-have, all persons and the circumflex are already linked to constructive feedback. Existing tasks target the meaning and negative order rather than an isolated dû lookup.

entries.source_title: Il est [adjectif] que + the subjunctive mood (Le Subjonctif) = It is [adjective] for [someone] to ... in French
entries.note: Evaluative adjectives versus affirmative certainty and general infinitives were already differentiated. Added optionality under n'est pas nécessaire so the adjective pattern is usable when a requirement is withdrawn.

entries.source_title: Conjugate pouvoir in the conditional past in French = could have (Le Conditionnel Passé)
entries.note: The existing lesson distinguishes missed opportunities from possible past explanations and actual ability. Full aurais...auraient pu forms and context-constrained tasks prevent an automatic non-occurrence inference.

entries.source_title: Conjugate regular -er, -ir, -dre verbs (+ avoir) in the future perfect in French (Le Futur Antérieur)
entries.note: Future completion, regular participles and every future avoir person already have contextual examples and independent formation. The future reference point is explained rather than inferred from a tense label.

entries.source_title: Conjugate avoir/être/faire and other irregular verbs in the future perfect in French (Le Futur Antérieur)
entries.note: Named irregular participles, including être's été with avoir, are already connected to the future auxiliary series and several constructed answers. Existing agreement guidance avoids adding duplicate verb-by-verb tables.

entries.source_title: Conjugate verbs (+ être) in the future perfect in French (Le Futur Antérieur)
entries.note: Future être formation, reflexive placement and movement exceptions are adequate. The public reflexive agreement shortcut is qualified by the course's direct/indirect-object rule rather than applied to every pronominal verb.

references.purpose: Checked direct versus indirect reflexive objects and the absence of automatic subject agreement.

entries.source_title: Conjugate vouloir/pouvoir/devoir in the future perfect in French (Le Futur Antérieur)
entries.note: Voulu/pu/dû already have full future-auxiliary formation, completed-future contexts and a separate conjectural-past interpretation. Modal meaning and temporal inference are explained without suggesting every form is common in conversation.

entries.source_title: Recognising être in the historic past in French (Le Passé Simple)
entries.note: The complete être historic-past series, fut/fût boundary and bounded narrative states already support recognition and everyday retelling. No forced literary speech production was added.

entries.source_title: Recognising faire in the historic past in French (Le Passé Simple)
entries.note: Every faire historic-past person is visible, with contextual decoding and conversion to ordinary narration. This meets the recognition need more usefully than increasing production of rare written forms.

entries.source_title: Recognising all -er verbs - including aller - in the historic past in French (Le Passé Simple)
entries.note: The -er series already includes aller, c/g spelling changes and narrative viewpoint. Learners identify and retell the forms, preserving the intended reading track rather than treating literary morphology as a TCF speaking target.

entries.source_title: Recognising -ir verbs in the historic past in French (Le Passé Simple)
entries.note: Regular -i-family recognition, partir transfer and an explicit warning that not every -ir verb follows it are already taught. Contextual retelling supplies the practical reading skill; the course does not claim an exhaustive exception dictionary.

entries.source_title: Conjugate s'asseoir in the future tense in French (Le Futur Simple)
entries.note: Both full future series of s'asseoir remain accepted, with reflexive placement, negation and sitting-down versus seated-state contrasts. Existing keys preserve the two legitimate spellings rather than choosing one as uniquely correct.

entries.source_title: Recognising avoir in the historic past in French (Le Passé Simple)
entries.note: The full eus...eurent series, eut/eût spelling distinction and ordinary-past retelling are already present. Recognition is integrated with narrative meaning rather than treated as decorative advanced production.

entries.source_title: Recognising regular -dre verbs in the historic past in French (Le Passé Simple)
entries.note: The complete vendre pattern transfers to attendre/répondre while explicitly excluding prendre. Independent decoding and retelling already address the useful regular-family boundary without conflating unlike forms.

entries.source_title: Conjugate verbs in the subjunctive past in French (Le Subjonctif Passé)
entries.note: Subjunctive auxiliaries, reflexive placement, agreement and negation are fully taught. Prior completion versus a future deadline and a current/later action already have contrasts; no extra literary tense is needed.

entries.source_title: Recognising voir/vivre in the historic past in French (Le Passé Simple)
entries.note: Both complete paradigms, the contextual ambiguity of vis and bounded long events already receive reading and retelling practice. The baseline correctly avoids treating every familiar-looking spelling as uniquely historic past.

entries.source_title: Recognising venir/tenir and derivatives in the historic past in French (Le Passé Simple)
entries.note: The -in- family and several derivatives already have full patterns and contextual recognition. The course explicitly prioritizes decoding and ordinary narration over unnecessary literary speaking drills.

entries.source_title: Conjugate vouloir in the imperative mood in French (L'Impératif)
entries.note: The public vous-only claim is too restrictive. Preserved both imperative series, common ne m'en veux pas and the elevated status of veuillons; Larousse confirms these distinctions, so no restrictive correction was made.

references.purpose: Read both imperative series, their register limits and common negative en vouloir constructions.

entries.source_title: Plus de ... que/Moins de ... que/Autant de ... que = More ... than/Less ... than/As much/many ... as (Comparisons with Nouns in French)
entries.note: Added two noun categories versus two holders, repeated de, stressed pronouns and full temporal comparison clauses. The source's absolute ban on verb repetition is not used; a full clause can clarify the comparison.

references.purpose: Checked that comparisons can introduce finite subordinate clauses; its optional ne discussion was not added as a new course requirement.

entries.source_title: Position of Double Pronouns in French - Direct Object Pronoun + Indirect Object Pronoun
entries.note: Ordering, placement and agreement were adequate, but clear reference needed more than an abstract rubric. Added competing antecedents and deliberate partial replacement; retained lui for either gender rather than a masculine-only gloss.

entries.source_title: Dans lequel/laquelle : alternative to où with places (French Relative Pronouns)
entries.note: The full spatial dans lequel series is already contrasted with time-relative où and other spatial relations. Constructed agreement and the explicit time boundary make this more than a list of interchangeable labels.

entries.source_title: Position of Double Pronouns in French - Reflexive Pronoun + Direct Object Pronoun
entries.note: First-slot reflexive pronouns and the change from following body-part object to preceding les are already explained together. Existing tasks require the resulting agreement, not only a memorized pronoun order.

entries.source_title: Tout ce qui/Tout ce que = All/everything that (French Relative Pronouns)
entries.note: Subject versus object function already determines tout ce qui/que, including an intervening object pronoun and elision. The learner is not told to decide solely from the next visible word.

entries.source_title: Position of Double Pronouns in French - Indirect Object Pronoun + "en"
entries.note: Person pronouns before en, elision and retained quantities already have meaningful examples and independently formed groups. The explanation distinguishes a de-complement from a counted quantity.

entries.source_title: Position of Double Pronouns in French - Direct Object Pronoun + "y"
entries.note: Le/la/les plus y was covered, but first/second-person direct objects were not exemplified. Added m'y, nous y and t'y in distinct meeting, transport and infinitive contexts, while retaining real complement-role analysis.

entries.source_title: Using [preposition] + qui/lequel/laquelle/etc = on what/behind whom/beside which/etc (French Relative Pronouns)
entries.note: Scoped the baseline named-thing rule and added neutral ce/quelque chose plus quoi and whole-event reference. The public blanket exclusion of relative quoi is not sustainable; the Académie also records less common nominal uses.

references.purpose: Checked relative quoi with neutral antecedents and whole statements, and less common nominal antecedents.

entries.source_title: Dont = Including/[quantity] of which (French Relative Pronouns)
entries.note: Retained valid full subset clauses without a second relative. Added the separate dont + quantity + qui/que construction and object agreement; the Académie supports full and shortened subsets, contrary to the source's mandatory-extra-relative claim.

references.purpose: Read full quantity clauses, shortened subsets and the manner use of dont; checked the claim that another relative is always required.

entries.source_title: Position of Double Pronouns in French - in affirmative commands in the imperative mood (L'Impératif)
entries.note: Affirmative/negative command order, elision, hyphens and linking-s ownership are already substantial. The source's blanket ban on en for people is not imported: OQLF explicitly permits person reference, including quantities.

references.purpose: Read person-reference examples and imperative double-pronoun order; checked the source's blanket exclusion of people.

entries.source_title: À + qui, auquel, à laquelle = to whom, what, which (French Relative Pronouns)
entries.note: The complete contracted à-series and à qui alternatives already follow the actual French verb's relationship. Every agreeing form is exercised and person alternatives remain accepted rather than arbitrarily restricted.

entries.source_title: De qui/dont/duquel = of/about whom, of/about which - with prepositional verbs with "de" (French Relative Pronouns)
entries.note: Simple de alternatives were taught, but clarification by inflection was abstract. Added genuinely competing person/institution antecedents and the limit when gender cannot disambiguate, with constrained referent-selection tasks.

entries.source_title: French reflexive pronouns can be used to express reciprocity - "each other"
entries.note: The dedicated lesson already distinguishes reciprocal from reflexive meaning and direct from indirect agreement. Its être rule remains tied to pronominal constructions, not every sentence expressing reciprocity; no blanket auxiliary rule was adopted.

references.purpose: Checked direct versus indirect reflexive objects and the absence of automatic subject agreement.

entries.source_title: Duquel/de laquelle/desquels/desquelles with prepositional phrases with "de" (French Relative Pronouns)
entries.note: The compound-preposition series was adequate. Added a plural-person de qui example and task rather than imposing the source's singular-only restriction, plus meaningful manière/façon dont teaching with independent retrieval.

references.purpose: Checked prepositional qui for person antecedents without a singular-only restriction.
Read full quantity clauses, shortened subsets and the manner use of dont; checked the claim that another relative is always required.

entries.source_title: Depuis que + [conjugated verb] = (Ever) since + [conjugated verb] in French
entries.note: Depuis que already distinguishes continuing present effects, completed starting events, past viewpoints and event counts. Contrast with bare duration depuis prevents a single-tense or compulsory-que rule.

entries.source_title: Malgré/En dépit de = Despite/In spite of in French
entries.note: Noun concession and de contractions were adequate. Added stressed-pronoun use and the semantic difference between malgré soi and malgré tout, so an involuntary reaction is not confused with persistence despite circumstances.

entries.source_title: Soit ... soit ... = Either ... or...
entries.note: Parallel nouns/phrases/infinitives/clauses and the fixed connector's independence from verb agreement are already explained. The course also avoids claiming that the connector alone settles every question of exclusivity.

entries.source_title: Pour que + the subjunctive mood (Le Subjonctif) = So that.../In order that... in French
entries.note: Purpose versus guaranteed result, subject control and pour + infinitive versus pour que + subjunctive already have contextual contrasts. Completed future goals are included without mistaking the subjunctive for a special future tense.

entries.source_title: Avant de + infinitive = Before + -ing in French
entries.note: The infinitive's understood subject, de elision and different-subject avant que are already explicit and exercised. Existing negative-infinitive teaching supplies pronoun placement; duplicating it here would not add a distinct decision.

entries.source_title: Dont = Whose (French Relative Pronouns)
entries.note: Possession already covers people and things, subject and object placement of the possessed noun, and suppression of redundant possessives. Constructed alternatives prevent an English whose-word-order shortcut.

entries.source_title: Bien que/quoique + the subjunctive mood (Le Subjonctif) = although/though in French
entries.note: Real-fact concession and present/past subjunctive were covered, but quoi que was only named. Added although versus whatever in meaningful contexts, including the different elisions, with independent discrimination and construction.

references.purpose: Checked relative quoi with neutral antecedents and whole statements, and less common nominal antecedents.

entries.source_title: Merci de / pour = Thank you for in French
entries.note: Kept both legitimate noun prepositions instead of a concrete-noun prohibition or automatic sarcasm inference. Added remercier's direct person object versus merci à, with noun/infinitive reasons and independent tasks; OQLF confirms the distinction.

references.purpose: Read the noun de/pour alternatives, infinitive de and merci recipient construction; checked a categorical concrete-noun rule.

entries.source_title: Forming the superlative of French adjectives in complex cases
entries.note: Repeated articles, adjective position, ordinal ranks, comparison sets and agreement already support full phrase construction. The same-person degree versus ranking contrast is also taught; the public comparison revealed no missing core decision.

entries.source_title: Ainsi que = as well as, just as vs the way that in French
entries.note: Addition versus manner and subject agreement were sound. Added equal-quality aussi bien que and the c'est ainsi que method frame, so learners do not map every English 'as well as' or 'that is how' to the additive construction.

entries.source_title: Ce, cet, cette, ces + [durée] -là/-ci = that/those or this/these + [duration] (French Demonstrative Adjectives)
entries.note: Determiner agreement and contextual -ci/-là reference were adequate. Added the scale of particular days versus an era, the année rather than an demonstrative pattern, and an explicitly future identified year.

entries.source_title: Faire + [infinitive] = to have something done in French (Causative)
entries.note: The dedicated causative lesson already exceeds a translation formula: arranger, performer and affected object are distinguished, with à/par, pronoun placement, unintended se faire and invariant fait. Contextual production already tests agency.

entries.source_title: "Penser/trouver/savoir/croire/prétendre que" are followed with the indicative mood (L'Indicatif) in affirmative sentences BUT with the subjunctive mood (Le Subjonctif) in negative ones
entries.note: Preserved the baseline indicative for newly learned facts after negative savoir and stance-constrained negative opinions. Larousse separately labels ne sache pas que as literary; it does not directly settle the entire modern negative-savoir contrast, so no broader reference-confirmation claim is made.

references.purpose: Checked the distinction between literary je ne sache pas que and ordinary savoir usage. This entry does not directly explain the full negative-savoir indicative contrast.

entries.source_title: Attendre quelqu'un vs s'attendre à quelque chose = to wait vs to expect in French
entries.note: Added waiting for an event versus anticipating it, a standard expected of someone, and s'y attendre. Positive expectations are explicitly possible; the lesson does not reduce expecting to apprehension or confuse it with scheduled-arrival attendre.

entries.source_title: Avoir besoin que + the subjunctive mood (Le Subjonctif) = To need someone to do something in French
entries.note: Besoin que versus besoin de was strong. Added a negative need and a need for someone not to act, with scoped negation and constructed tasks; lack of necessity is not presented as a prohibition.

entries.source_title: Expressing "the most/least that I have (ever)..." with a superlative followed by the subjunctive mood in French (Le Subjonctif)
entries.note: Retained evaluation versus factual assertion, completed/current time and jamais as ever. The choice is not reduced to whether the listener knows the referent; OQLF confirms a subjunctive preference with context-dependent indicative possibilities.

references.purpose: Checked context-dependent relative mood and the preference, not universal obligation, for subjunctive after superlatives.

entries.source_title: Expressing "the day after/the day before" in French with "demain/hier" vs "le lendemain/la veille" vs "le jour suivant/le jour précédent" (French Expressions of Time)
entries.note: Speaker versus narrative reference was adequate. Added event-noun complements and contractions, previous evening, conversational day-relative wording and adjective précédent versus participial précédant, with independent construction rather than date substitutions alone.

entries.source_title: Using negations with infinitive verbs in French indirect speech (French Negations)
entries.note: Simple and past infinitive negation already distinguishes pas/plus/jamais/rien from personne and preserves pronoun groups. Both legitimate negative past-infinitive orders are taught and accepted where relevant.

entries.source_title: Comment ça se fait/Comment se fait-il que... ? = How come/How is it that...? (French Questions)
entries.note: Formal inversion with conventional subjunctive, conversational factual questions, standalone how-come and the no-extra-t spelling are already contrasted. Register is contextual, and the baseline correctly avoids rejecting conversational indicative automatically.
